_comment: The WINDOW-BASE rule, as a table both languages must satisfy.
A client's message store is a paginated newest-first window, so its own turn
projection cannot know how many turns precede the window's first message. It is
told: `GET /api/chats/{id}` answers `turn_offset` and `turn_segment_closed`, and
`offset + 1` is the session-absolute ordinal of the window's first turn.
This file is the contract between the two halves. It is read by
TestTurnWindowBaseContract (Go, over turnWindowBase) and by turns.node.test.ts
(TypeScript, over projectTurns with a base). Changing the boundary rule in one
language fails the other language's test, which is the only mechanism keeping
them in agreement — there is no code generation for behaviour.
`messages` is one persisted message array. `blocks` lists one subtask id per
block; absent means the message carries no blocks at all, which is what every
row predating the step rule needs. `windows` lists the cuts: `start` is the
index the window begins at, `turn_offset` and `turn_segment_closed` are what the
server must answer for it, and `n` is the absolute ordinal expected for each
turn the window's own projection produces.
TWO SPLITS ARE THE REASON `turn_segment_closed` EXISTS, and both are named in
the table below: a window opening on a STEP-ONLY message and one opening on an
EVENT row carrying no outcome. `opensHeaderlessTurn` returns false for either,
so each CONTINUES the closed turn before it — and a local scan seeded
`closed: false` instead reads the next assistant message as joining that
fragment rather than opening a turn of its own, which shifts every later
ordinal. Drop the seed and those two rows go red; drop the
continues-a-turn subtraction from the offset and every mid-turn split does.
The EMPTY window (`start` past the last message) is rendered by nothing, and it
is pinned so the value is deliberate rather than accidental: it reports the
state after the whole array, which is what a `before_id` naming the first
message asks for.

cut MID-TURN, so the window's first turn is the one it continues
an empty window reports the state after the whole array

cases.name: a window opening on a STEP-ONLY message after a closed turn
_comment: The divergent case the seed exists for. `isStepMessage` makes
`opensHeaderlessTurn` false, so s1 CONTINUES turn 1 — and the next assistant
message opens turn 2 only because the segment is still closed. Seeded false,
the local scan reads a2 as joining s1's fragment and answers ONE turn.

windows.name: cut on the step message, which continues turn 1
cut on the assistant message the step message precedes

cases.name: a window opening on an EVENT row carrying no outcome
_comment: The second divergent shape: a non-assistant row with no `turn_outcome` fails
both clauses of `opensHeaderlessTurn`, so it joins the closed turn before it
and the assistant message after it opens the next one.

windows.name: cut on the event row, which continues turn 1
cut on the assistant message after it

cases.name: a mid-turn STEER joins the turn already running
_comment: `isPrompt` is false for a steer, so it may not open a turn — and it carries no
`turn_outcome`, so a window opening on one is a third continues-a-turn shape.

windows.name: cut on the steer, which continues turn 1
cut on the reply the steer was read into

cases.name: a transcript that begins agent-initiated
_comment: The first message opens a turn whatever it carries, so a window at 0 has no
offset and no closed segment behind it — which is exactly what the default
base a whole-session projection uses must answer.

windows.name: cut on the prompt after it
